readerTitle: The accounting firm that stopped marketing to everyone
caseNote: 가상 사례 (소규모 회계 사무소, 가정 청소 업체) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 전문 서비스 마케팅은 더 크게 외치는 일이 아니다. 누구에게 말할지 좁히고, 고객이 어느 단계에서 멈추는지 찾아 그 지점을 고치는 일이다.
misconception: 회계처럼 신뢰가 중요한 서비스는 대상을 넓게 잡고 광고를 늘리면 고객이 늘어난다.

sources.text: 이 유닛의 개념 레슨: 세분화·표적·포지셔닝(MKT-01-03), 퍼널(MKT-01-04)
모든 수치와 인물은 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 퍼널 계산 확인: 방문 400 → 체크리스트 다운로드 30 (7.5%) → 상담 예약 12 (30÷12 기준 40%) → 계약 2 (12명 중 약 17%). 상담 후 계약하지 않은 사람 10명.
특정 국가의 세법·회계 규정은 언급하지 않도록 식당 관련 업무를 '급여, 팁, 식자재 원가'처럼 일반적인 표현으로만 적었습니다. 게시 전 국가별 규정처럼 읽히는 문장이 없는지 다시 확인하세요.

cards.title: The accounting firm that stopped marketing to everyone
body: Priya runs a four-person accounting firm. Her website says: *Trusted accounting for individuals and businesses.*
Each spring the phone rings with people asking one question: "How much for a tax return?" They compare three quotes and pick the cheapest. The rest of the year, it's quiet.

image.label: Accountant at a desk with a ringing phone and a stack of identical quotes
image.brief: 따뜻한 일러스트. 작은 회계 사무소 책상에서 여성 회계사가 울리는 전화를 보고 있고, 옆에 똑같이 생긴 견적서 세 장이 겹쳐 있음. 창밖은 봄. 실제 로고나 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: What should Priya change first?
body: She has a small budget and wants steady, year-round clients, not one-off spring jobs. Several of her best clients own local restaurants.

options.text: Run more online ads with the same message
options.feedback: More people would hear "trusted accounting for everyone," which sounds like every other firm. Ads buy attention, but they don't fix a message that gives people no reason to choose her.

options.text: Focus on independent restaurant owners and say so plainly
options.feedback: This is **segment, target, position** at work. Picking one group lets her speak to their exact problems, so she stops being one of three quotes.

options.text: Cut her price to win the spring price shoppers
options.feedback: She might win more spring jobs, but she'd be competing on the one thing that makes clients leave next year for someone cheaper.

cards.title: "For everyone" sounds like no one.
body: Priya **segments** her market by type of business, **targets** independent restaurants, and rewrites her message: *Accountants for independent restaurants. We handle payroll for shift staff, tips and food costs, so you can run the kitchen.*
That line does two jobs. Restaurant owners feel understood. Everyone else can see quickly that she's not for them, which saves both sides time.
She now writes a short guide on reading a restaurant's monthly numbers and shares it with local restaurant groups.

cards.title: Three months later, follow the owners.
body: The new message brings the right people. But only 2 of 400 become clients. The **funnel** shows each step a buyer passes, and where they stop.

breakdown.label: Become clients
breakdown.detail: 10 people talk to Priya, then say no

cards.softwareNote: A bookkeeping app has the same funnel: site visits, free signups, active trials, paid plans. The work is the same too. Find the step with the biggest drop before buying more traffic.

cards.title: Where should Priya put her effort now?

options.text: Double the budget to get more visitors to the guide
options.feedback: More people would enter the funnel, but most would still leak out at the same spot. She'd pay more for each client she wins.

options.text: Ask the 10 owners who didn't sign what held them back
options.feedback: The **funnel** points to the step from call to client. That's where interested owners stop, so fixing it raises results without new traffic.

options.text: Redesign the website to boost downloads
options.feedback: Downloads could rise, but the bigger drop comes after people have already talked to her. A nicer site won't fix that.

cards.title: The fear wasn't price. It was switching.
body: Priya calls the owners who said no. Most had the same worry: changing accountants in the middle of the year sounded messy, and they feared surprise bills.
So she changes the offer, not the ads. She moves their records herself, handles the switch for them, and charges one fixed monthly fee.
Over the next three months, more of her calls turn into clients. Each one is a year-round client, not a spring job.

cards.title: Narrow and slow can still be right.
body: Focusing works only if the group is big enough and easy to reach. Five restaurants in a small town may not sustain a firm. Focus also doesn't mean turning others away. It means aiming your message at one group.
Trust-heavy services move slowly. An owner may read the guide in May and call in October. With numbers this small, judge each step over months, not weeks, and talk to people, not just counts.

cards.title: Now it's a house-cleaning company.
body: Leo's cleaning business advertises "cleaning for any home." He gets plenty of quote requests through his website, but few turn into bookings. He often replies a day or two later.
Which plan uses both ideas best?

options.text: Target busy families with pets, and reply to every quote request within an hour
options.feedback: A clear target sharpens the message, and the funnel shows the leak sits between request and booking. Fast replies fix the step where people already stall.

options.text: Hand out flyers across town offering 20% off
options.feedback: It adds more requests at the top while the slow replies keep losing them. And the discount attracts price shoppers, not regulars.

options.text: Get a new logo and a fresh website
options.feedback: It may look more professional, but it doesn't choose a customer or fix the slow replies that lose bookings.

cards.title: Choose who it's for, then fix where they stop.
body: This lesson used two ideas. **Segment, target, position** gave Priya a message one group could recognize. **The funnel** showed her that the leak was after the call, not before it.
**Try it today:** write one sentence naming who your business is for. Then count how many people reached each step last month, and circle the biggest drop.
